hero.headline: Federal judge blocks Postal Service restrictions on mail-in ballot delivery
hero.body:
A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting across the United States, preventing the Postal Service from implementing a plan that would have denied ballots to voters in states refusing to turn over their voter rolls to the federal government.

Judge Emmet Sullivan of the US District Court for the District of Columbia ruled against the restriction, marking the second time that a plan to limit mail ballots across the country has faced a court setback.

The blocked restriction stemmed from an order targeting mail-in voting access. Civil rights groups, including the NAACP, challenged the proposed changes in court, arguing that the Postal Service directive would create barriers to voting. Multiple organizations joined the legal challenge, contending that the restrictions would make it harder for Americans to cast ballots by mail, particularly affecting communities that depend heavily on mail-in voting.

Mail-in voting has become a significant method of casting ballots in recent election cycles, with millions of Americans relying on the option. Voting rights advocates had opposed the proposed changes, saying they would create unnecessary obstacles for voters without good cause.

The judge's order keeps current mail ballot handling procedures in place while the case continues through the courts. The ruling ensures that existing practices for delivering mail ballots remain unchanged for now, preventing the implementation of the proposed restrictions.

The decision represents a significant setback for efforts to limit mail-in voting access. Judge Sullivan found sufficient grounds to block the restriction, siding with those who argued the changes would harm voting access.

This case is part of a broader legal battle over voting access and election administration that has intensified in recent years. As states prepare for upcoming elections, courts continue to weigh competing claims about voting methods and election security. The block demonstrates ongoing judicial skepticism toward restrictions on mail-in voting, with multiple courts now rejecting similar proposals.

The outcome comes amid heightened focus on election procedures and voting access. Legal challenges to voting restrictions have become common in the current political environment, with courts frequently called upon to determine the constitutionality of various election administration policies.

The Postal Service has not yet announced whether it will appeal the ruling. If appealed, the case could move to higher courts, potentially reaching the appellate level. The decision ensures that the current mail ballot system continues operating under existing rules while legal proceedings advance.

The ruling highlights how courts are actively shaping election policy through litigation. As voting access remains a contested issue, this decision will likely influence other ongoing legal battles over mail-in voting procedures and voter eligibility requirements across the country.

cards.headline: US and Iran conclude indirect talks in Doha with positive progress on Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: Negotiations in Qatar focused on reducing tensions in the strategic waterway ahead of Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran wrapped up indirect talks in Doha on Thursday, with Qatari mediators reporting positive progress. The negotiations focused primarily on the Strait of Hormuz, the critical shipping lane where tensions had escalated in recent weeks. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner led the American delegation in the discussions.

The talks come as Iran prepares for the funeral of Ayatollah Khamenei, with both sides appearing to seek reduced tensions in the strategic waterway through which a significant portion of global oil supplies pass. Qatar served as the mediator for the indirect negotiations, hosting both delegations separately to facilitate communication between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Russia launches major missile and drone strikes on Kyiv, killing at least eight
cards.body:
Russia struck Kyiv with a large-scale missile and drone attack early Thursday, killing at least eight people and injuring five others. The strikes set residential buildings ablaze across the Ukrainian capital in what officials described as the biggest assault on the city in weeks. Strong explosions rocked Kyiv hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Moscow was planning a massive attack.

Multiple residential buildings were hit in the strikes, which involved both missiles and drones. Emergency crews worked to extinguish fires and search for survivors amid the damaged structures. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed that residential areas bore the brunt of the assault, which caused widespread damage across several districts of the capital.

The timing of the attack followed Zelensky's public warning about an impending major Russian offensive. Ukrainian air defense systems engaged the incoming missiles and drones, though several projectiles reached their targets. The scale of the assault marked a significant escalation in attacks on the capital, which had seen reduced strike activity in recent weeks compared to earlier phases of the conflict.

The strike comes as Russia continues its military campaign in Ukraine, with periodic intensification of attacks on major urban centers. Kyiv has been targeted repeatedly throughout the war, though the frequency and intensity of strikes on the capital have varied. Thursday's attack represented one of the most significant assaults on the city in recent months, both in terms of casualties and the volume of missiles and drones deployed.

Ukrainian authorities continue to assess the full extent of the damage from the strikes. Rescue operations were ongoing as emergency services worked to ensure no additional casualties remained trapped in damaged buildings. The attack underscores the continued vulnerability of Ukrainian cities to Russian missile and drone strikes, despite air defense systems that have intercepted many incoming threats throughout the conflict.

cards.headline: Heat Wave Strains US Power Grid as Demand Reaches Record Levels
cards.body:
The largest power grid in the United States issued an emergency alert as a widespread heat wave pushed electricity demand to unprecedented levels. PJM Interconnection, which serves 65 million people across 13 states and the District of Columbia, warned that its system was stretched to capacity as temperatures soared across the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions.

The grid operator reported price spikes and urged conservation measures to prevent potential blackouts. The emergency comes as air conditioning use surges during one of the earliest and most intense heat waves on record for the region. PJM manages the flow of electricity across an area stretching from Illinois to New Jersey.

Energy experts pointed to increased strain on power systems from more frequent and severe heat waves. Data centers in particular have drawn scrutiny for their electricity consumption during peak demand periods. Residents living near data center facilities expressed concern about the facilities' contribution to grid stress during extreme weather events.

The grid emergency highlights growing challenges facing electrical infrastructure as climate patterns shift. Power systems designed for historical weather patterns face increasing pressure from extreme heat events that drive air conditioning demand higher. Grid operators have increasingly issued conservation appeals during summer months as peak demand periods have grown longer and more intense.

PJM officials provided operational updates throughout the emergency period, detailing the steps taken to maintain grid stability. The operator coordinates electricity generation and transmission across its coverage area, balancing supply and demand in real time. The current heat wave represents a test of the grid's capacity during a period when electrical demand for cooling has reached levels that strain available generation resources.

cards.headline: White House Moves Forward With AI Model Standards
cards.teaser: The administration is accelerating plans to establish standards for artificial intelligence models through discussions with technology companies.
cards.body:
The White House is advancing plans to create standards for artificial intelligence models, according to reports. The administration has entered discussions with AI companies regarding voluntary model standards as part of the regulatory framework.

The development comes amid growing scrutiny of AI governance approaches. Industry observers noted divisions emerging within the technology sector over regulatory approaches, with different factions advocating for varying levels of oversight and standardization.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Title IX ruling may open door to damages in transgender athlete cases
cards.teaser: Legal experts say the court's recent decision could affect lawsuits brought by women impacted by policies allowing transgender athletes in women's sports.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court's recent ruling on Title IX could have implications for lawsuits seeking damages from women affected by transgender athletes competing in women's sports. The decision represents a win for Republican lawmakers who have pushed for restrictions, while most Democratic officials have remained quiet on the matter.

The ruling caps a year of legal setbacks for transgender advocates on sports-related issues. The NCAA leadership stated there are no plans to change existing rules on transgender athletes despite the Supreme Court decision. Legal analysts are examining how the ruling might affect pending cases brought by female athletes challenging policies that allow transgender women to compete in women's categories.

cards.headline: Northeast braces for extreme heat through July 4 weekend
cards.teaser: Record-breaking temperatures are forecast across the Northeast and Midwest through Independence Day.
cards.body:
The Northeast is preparing for a dangerous heat wave that will peak during Fourth of July celebrations. Temperatures are forecast to reach life-threatening levels across seven cities, with meteorologists warning of record-breaking heat through the holiday weekend.

In response to the extreme conditions, emergency heat protocols have been activated in the New York City area and Connecticut. Officials are urging residents to take precautions during outdoor Independence Day activities as the intense weather pattern affects the region.

cards.headline: Venezuela struggles to recover and bury bodies as earthquake death toll rises
cards.teaser: Thousands of bodies have overwhelmed the country's forensic system, turning a seaport into a temporary morgue.
cards.body:
Venezuela continues to grapple with the aftermath of last week's earthquakes as the death toll mounts and recovery efforts strain the nation's capacity. Thousands of bodies have overwhelmed the forensic system, forcing authorities to convert a seaport into a temporary morgue to handle the massive number of casualties.

Rescue workers continue to search for survivors in the rubble, with a two-year-old boy named Kleiber Moran pulled from the debris on Wednesday, six days after the earthquakes struck. His aunt told the BBC she would provide him with a mother's warmth as he recovers. The disaster has created a humanitarian crisis as the country works to identify victims and provide proper burials while simultaneously searching for any remaining survivors.

cards.headline: Traditionalist Catholic group ordains four bishops in defiance of Pope Leo XIV
cards.teaser: The Society of St. Pius X proceeded with the ceremony despite Vatican warnings of excommunication.
cards.body:
The Society of St. Pius X proceeded with the ordination of four bishops in Switzerland despite Vatican warnings of automatic excommunication. Thousands of worshippers attended the ceremony in the Swiss Alps as part of the breakaway group's defiant action.

The ordinations represent a serious breach of Catholic Church law, as bishops cannot be consecrated without papal approval. The Vatican has cautioned that the action risks formalizing a schism within the Church. The Society of St. Pius X has long operated in irregular canonical status, opposing reforms implemented by the Vatican.

cards.headline: Afghan migrants accuse Turkish police of beatings and abandonment in freezing conditions
cards.teaser: Young migrants say they were stripped, had their hands tied, and lost limbs to frostbite after encountering authorities.
cards.body:
Young Afghan migrants traveling toward Europe have accused Turkish police of beating them with iron rods and leaving them in freezing temperatures. According to their accounts, officers stripped them of clothing and tied their hands while exposed to severe cold.

The migrants suffered frostbite severe enough to cause limb loss. These allegations add to concerns about how refugees and asylum seekers are treated while transiting through Turkey, a major route for those fleeing Afghanistan and other conflict-affected regions.

cards.headline: England advances in World Cup after defeating Congo 2-1
cards.teaser: Congo spent most of the match leading before England scored twice to secure victory.
cards.body:
England defeated Congo 2-1 on Wednesday night in World Cup competition, staging a comeback after spending much of the game trailing. Congo led for the majority of the match before England's late rally secured the win and advancement in the tournament.

The loss proved devastating for Congo fans, who had watched their team control the game for extended periods. The match represented a significant moment for the Congolese national team, which had been on the verge of a major upset against one of the tournament favorites before the late collapse.

cards.headline: English flag sparks debate over national identity during World Cup celebrations
cards.teaser: The St. George's Cross has been widely displayed by soccer fans but has caused tension over what it represents.
cards.body:
England's St. George's Cross—a white banner bearing a bold red cross—has become a flashpoint during World Cup celebrations. Soccer fans have displayed the flag throughout the tournament, but its prominence has sparked questions about national representation and identity.

The debate reflects deeper tensions in England about patriotism and national symbols in a diverse society. While some supporters view the flag as unifying backing for the national team, others contend its display has become linked to specific political and social viewpoints, raising questions about who the symbol truly represents.

cards.headline: Colorado governor fires clemency board members who opposed freeing Tina Peters
cards.teaser: Governor Jared Polis removed officials from the clemency board after they publicly criticized his decision to free the convicted election official.
cards.body:
Colorado Governor Jared Polis has fired members of the state clemency board who spoke out against his decision to grant clemency to Tina Peters. Peters, who was convicted for her role in election-related offenses, received clemency from Polis despite opposition from legal experts on the board.

The dismissed board members had publicly criticized the governor's decision to free Peters, who had been convicted for election-related crimes. The firings have drawn criticism from observers who characterized the move as retaliatory against officials who exercised independent judgment in opposing the clemency decision for the convicted election official.

cards.headline: EMS responded to Senator Mitch McConnell's home for cardiac arrest last month
cards.teaser: Emergency medical services were called to the senator's residence for an unconscious patient, recordings indicate.
cards.body:
Paramedics responded to a cardiac arrest call at Senator Mitch McConnell's home last month, according to emergency service recordings. The recordings suggest EMS was dispatched for an unconscious patient on the day McConnell was hospitalized.

McConnell's health has become a subject of attention in Washington as the senator has been absent from recent proceedings. The emergency response occurred at his residence before he was rushed to the hospital. McConnell's office has not provided detailed information about the incident or his current health status.

cards.teaser: Legal experts say the court's recent decision could affect lawsuits brought by women impacted by policies allowing transgender athletes in women's sports.

cards.headline: FBI says some Nancy Guthrie ransom notes were genuine extortion attempts
cards.teaser: The bureau clarified it is investigating certain demands as legitimate after initially determining some notes were fakes.
cards.body:
The FBI is investigating extortion demands connected to Nancy Guthrie's disappearance that "may potentially be legitimate," the agency announced Wednesday. This clarification followed a Reuters report identifying three kidnapping notes in the case as fabricated.

While some ransom communications have been determined to be fake, the FBI is treating other extortion attempts as credible threats requiring active investigation.

cards.headline: Trump takes first flight aboard retrofitted Qatari jet as Air Force One
cards.teaser: The president flew to North Dakota aboard the newly configured aircraft received as a gift from Qatar.
cards.body:
President Trump made his inaugural flight aboard a new Air Force One, a retrofitted jet originally given to the United States by Qatar. The aircraft was used for a trip to North Dakota for the debut of a library honoring a noted outdoorsman.

The jet has undergone modifications to serve as a presidential aircraft. Reporters who were aboard the maiden flight documented the trip. The use of the Qatari-gifted aircraft as Air Force One marks a change in the presidential fleet configuration.

cards.headline: Apple Lobbies to Purchase Memory Chips From Chinese Manufacturers
cards.teaser: Apple is pursuing negotiations to buy memory chips from Chinese companies CXMT and YMTC amid supply constraints and pricing pressures.
cards.body:
Apple has entered discussions to purchase memory chips from two Chinese manufacturers, CXMT and YMTC, according to reports. The move comes as memory and storage chip prices have increased, creating supply challenges for the technology company.

Analysts suggested the negotiations reflect efforts to address supply constraints driven by artificial intelligence hardware demands rather than purely cost considerations. The chip supply crunch has intensified as AI applications require increasing amounts of memory and storage capacity across the technology industry.

cards.headline: Bending Spoons Raises $1 Billion in US Market Debut
cards.teaser: The Italian company that owns AOL and Vimeo saw shares surge nearly 40% in its first day of trading after an initial public offering valued at $18 billion.
cards.body:
Bending Spoons completed a $1 billion initial public offering on US markets, with shares jumping nearly 40% during the company's trading debut. The Italian software firm, which owns internet properties including AOL, Vimeo, and Evernote, achieved an $18 billion valuation through the offering.

The company's founder discussed the IPO success, attributing the business approach to minimizing reliance on luck through systematic processes. The public offering marks a significant milestone for the Milan-based company, which has acquired numerous legacy internet brands in recent years.

cards.headline: White House Moves Forward With AI Model Standards
cards.teaser: The administration is accelerating plans to establish standards for artificial intelligence models through discussions with technology companies.
cards.body:
The White House is advancing plans to create standards for artificial intelligence models, according to reports. The administration has entered discussions with AI companies regarding voluntary model standards as part of the regulatory framework.

The development comes amid growing scrutiny of AI governance approaches. Industry observers noted divisions emerging within the technology sector over regulatory approaches, with different factions advocating for varying levels of oversight and standardization.

cards.headline: SEC Investigates Alleged Insider Trading Scheme Costing Susquehanna Millions
cards.teaser: Securities regulators are probing claims that insider trades related to Chinese brokerage enforcement actions generated $100 million in profits.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission opened an investigation into alleged insider trading that cost trading firm Susquehanna International significant losses. The firm claims that insiders made $100 million trading on advance knowledge of Chinese government enforcement actions against brokerage FUTU.

Susquehanna obtained a court order to freeze accounts and subpoena brokers as part of its case. The trading firm alleges that individuals with advance knowledge of the regulatory crackdown profited from positions taken before the public announcement, while Susquehanna and other market participants sustained losses.

cards.headline: US Auto Sales Show Mixed Results in Second Quarter
cards.teaser: Automakers reported varied sales performance as hybrid vehicles gained market share despite high gasoline prices and affordability concerns.
cards.body:
Major automakers reported mixed second-quarter sales results for the US market. Hybrid vehicles emerged as a bright spot, delivering strong performance and bolstering overall sales figures. Despite elevated gasoline prices hovering near $4 per gallon, consumers continued purchasing vehicles, demonstrating resilience in the market.

Affordability remains a significant challenge for buyers as economic pressures persist. Some established automakers lost ground to competitors during the quarter, reflecting shifting consumer preferences and competitive dynamics within the industry.

cards.headline: California Bans Sell By Labels on Food Products
cards.teaser: A new state law eliminates sell by dates on food packaging to reduce waste and clarify expiration labeling for consumers.
cards.body:
California implemented a ban on sell by labels on food products, changing how retailers and manufacturers mark expiration information. The law took effect July 1 and aims to reduce food waste by eliminating confusing date labels that lead consumers to discard safe food.

The legislation standardizes food dating practices by focusing on best by and use by designations. Major retailers including Walmart have begun adjusting their stocking and labeling practices to comply with the new California requirements.

hero.headline: NASA plans mission to rescue aging Swift telescope from decaying orbit
hero.body:
NASA is preparing a mission to save the Swift telescope, which has been studying gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena since 2004. The spacecraft has begun sinking toward Earth as its orbit decays, prompting the agency to plan a rendezvous mission that would boost the telescope back to a higher, more stable orbit.

The rescue effort, dubbed the Swift Boost mission, represents a rare attempt to physically reposition an aging space telescope rather than allowing it to fall back into the atmosphere. The mission combines scientific preservation with an opportunity to test techniques that could have applications for national defense satellites. NASA has characterized the operation as a daring maneuver that will require precise coordination in orbit.

Swift has operated for more than two decades beyond its original five-year mission timeline, making significant contributions to astronomy by detecting and studying gamma-ray bursts, which are among the most energetic events in the universe. The telescope's orbital altitude has gradually decreased over time due to atmospheric drag, a common phenomenon for spacecraft in low Earth orbit. Without intervention, the telescope would eventually reenter the atmosphere and be destroyed.

The planned boost mission will need to be executed before the telescope's orbit decays to a point where rescue becomes impossible. NASA officials have not disclosed a specific launch date for the mission but have indicated they are working under time constraints. The operation will test capabilities that could prove valuable for extending the lives of other satellites or repositioning them as needed.

The rescue effort reflects NASA's broader strategy of maximizing the scientific return from existing space assets. Extending Swift's operational life would allow continued observations that complement newer telescopes and provide valuable long-term data sets. The mission also offers a practical demonstration of orbital servicing techniques that the agency and the Department of Defense have been developing for future applications.

cards.headline: Scientists discover planet that survived its star's death
cards.teaser: Researchers using the Webb telescope identified aerosols and hydrocarbons in the atmosphere of a planet orbiting a white dwarf star.
cards.body:
Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope have studied a planet that survived the violent death of its star, providing new insights into how planetary systems might endure stellar evolution. The research team detected aerosols and hydrocarbons in the planet's atmosphere as it orbits a white dwarf, the dense remnant left behind after a star exhausts its fuel and sheds its outer layers.

The discovery offers clues about Earth's potential fate when the sun eventually becomes a red giant in billions of years. New models suggest that whether Earth survives depends on a delicate balance of factors during the sun's expansion phase. The planet observed by Webb demonstrates that some worlds can persist through their star's transformation, offering scientists a rare opportunity to study post-stellar-death planetary conditions.

cards.headline: Apple preparing new iPad Pro and MacBook Pro releases for 2027
cards.teaser: The company is readying updated iPad Pro tablets and planning a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro, according to reports.
cards.body:
Apple is working on a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro expected to launch in the first half of 2027. The company is also testing four new iPad Pro models set to arrive in spring 2027, with a focus on internal improvements rather than major design changes.

Apple's professional computing lineup continues to evolve as the company advances its transition to Apple Silicon. The updated MacBook Pro will bring visual changes to the entry-level tier, while the iPad Pro updates represent the company's ongoing iteration of its tablet offerings.

cards.headline: Xbox testing feature to convert physical games to digital copies
cards.teaser: Microsoft is experimenting with a disc-to-digital program that would allow players to digitize their physical game collections.
cards.body:
Microsoft has been quietly developing a disc-to-digital feature that would allow Xbox owners to convert their physical game collections into digital versions. The capability would apply to games from the Xbox One era and beyond.

The feature aligns with Microsoft's broader strategy to move away from physical media. Sony has already begun this transition, announcing plans to stop releasing new PlayStation games on disc starting in January 2028.

cards.headline: Bending Spoons surges 40% in first day of public trading
cards.teaser: The Italian software company, which has acquired brands like AOL, Evernote, and Vimeo, defied expectations in its stock market debut.
cards.body:
Bending Spoons gained 40 percent on its first day of trading following an $18 billion initial public offering. The Milan-based company has built its business by acquiring and revamping established internet brands including AOL, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, and Vimeo.

The strong debut stands out amid broader weakness in the software-as-a-service sector. The company's co-founders attribute their success to a strategy focused on minimizing the role of luck in business outcomes, drawing lessons from an earlier startup failure.

cards.headline: WhatsApp usernames raise concerns about impersonation risks
cards.teaser: Meta introduced usernames to improve privacy, but critics question whether safeguards can prevent users from being impersonated.
cards.body:
WhatsApp's new username feature has sparked concerns about impersonation as users begin adopting the handles. Meta introduced usernames as a privacy enhancement, allowing people to connect without sharing phone numbers, but the rollout has raised questions about how effectively the company can prevent bad actors from creating deceptive accounts.

Critics are questioning whether Meta's safeguards are adequate to prevent impersonation at scale. The feature represents a significant change to how WhatsApp functions, moving away from its phone-number-only identification system. The company has not detailed all the measures it plans to use to verify identities and prevent abuse of the username system.

cards.headline: T-Mobile migrating tens of thousands of virtual machines off VMware
cards.teaser: The telecommunications company is moving infrastructure away from VMware while pursuing legal action against Broadcom.
cards.body:
T-Mobile is moving tens of thousands of virtual machines off VMware infrastructure amid an ongoing lawsuit with Broadcom, which acquired VMware. The migration represents a significant technical undertaking for the telecommunications company as it shifts away from the virtualization platform.

T-Mobile wants Broadcom to continue supporting its VMware perpetual licenses, but has begun the process of moving workloads regardless of the legal outcome. The dispute reflects broader tensions in the enterprise software market following Broadcom's acquisition of VMware and subsequent changes to licensing terms that have affected many corporate customers.

hero.headline: US advances to World Cup round of 16 after 2-0 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina
hero.body:
The United States men's national team defeated Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium to advance to the round of 16. The victory marks the first time the US has won a World Cup knockout match in 24 years.

The match took a dramatic turn when forward Folarin Balogun was sent off after a collision with Bosnia-Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic. The incident, which saw Balogun's foot land on his opponent's ankle, drew immediate controversy. US players and coach Mauricio Pochettino reacted with visible disbelief to the red card decision, which left the team playing with 10 men for the remainder of the match.

Despite the numerical disadvantage and the tension that followed, the US held firm defensively. Malik Tillman helped secure the victory with a crucial contribution in the second half. The team's ability to maintain composure and control the game while down a player proved decisive.

The red card has sparked widespread discussion about whether FIFA might overturn the decision on appeal. Multiple news outlets have examined the protocols available to the USMNT, as a suspension would prevent Balogun from playing in the round of 16 match if it stands. The incident has also prompted analysis of VAR review procedures and whether protocols were properly applied during the decision-making process.

The US will face Belgium in the next round after the European side completed a remarkable comeback victory over Senegal. Belgium won 3-2 in extra time, with Youri Tielemans scoring a late penalty following a VAR review. That penalty decision also generated controversy, though Belgium's comeback from an early deficit showcased the team's resilience.

The matchup between the US and Belgium will test the American side against a proven European opponent. Belgium's ability to mount a comeback despite falling behind early suggests they remain a dangerous threat despite questions about their consistency in recent tournaments.

The victory represents an important achievement for the US program as it continues rebuilding its presence on the world stage. The team's capacity to overcome adversity, particularly playing effectively with reduced numbers, demonstrates the mental strength Mauricio Pochettino has been developing in the squad. Advancing past the round of 32 keeps the team's World Cup campaign alive and sets up a challenging encounter against a team that proved it can turn matches around even when facing significant obstacles.

The temperature had risen during the match at the Bay Area stadium, which had featured a pro-USA crowd from the start. Bosnia-Herzegovina brought supporters from their diaspora communities across Germany, Austria, Sweden, Switzerland and the United States, creating a passionate atmosphere on both sides.

cards.headline: Celtics trade Jaylen Brown to 76ers for Paul George
cards.teaser: Boston has sent All-Star guard Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George and draft picks in a blockbuster trade.
cards.body:
The Boston Celtics have traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George, two first-round picks, and two second-round picks.

Brown, who had expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics, will join Joel Embiid in Philadelphia. Boston adds George to pair alongside Jayson Tatum as the franchise looks to reshape its roster following the blockbuster deal.

cards.headline: Belgium rallies past Senegal on late extra-time penalty to reach round of 16
cards.teaser: Youri Tielemans converted a penalty late in extra time to complete Belgium's comeback from two goals down against Senegal.
cards.body:
Belgium mounted a remarkable comeback from 2-0 down, scoring two late goals to force extra time against Senegal. The match was decided deep in extra time when Youri Tielemans converted a penalty following a VAR review, securing a 3-2 victory. The penalty came after a review determined that Lamine Kamara had fouled Tielemans moments before Dodi Lukebakio's shot skimmed the crossbar.

The winning goal at 124 minutes and 44 seconds marked the latest goal in World Cup history. Belgium's stunning comeback has drawn both praise and controversy, particularly surrounding the penalty decision. Belgium will next face the United States in the round of 16.

cards.headline: Folarin Balogun receives red card in US win over Bosnia-Herzegovina
cards.teaser: The US forward was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic during their World Cup knockout match.
cards.body:
Folarin Balogun scored for the United States before being sent off with a straight red card during their 2-0 World Cup victory over Bosnia-Herzegovina in Santa Clara. The dismissal came after a collision with Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemović in which Balogun's foot landed on his opponent's ankle.

The red card proved controversial, with coach Mauricio Pochettino and players expressing disbelief at the decision. Despite playing with a numerical disadvantage, the US advanced to the last 16, with Malik Tillman scoring to seal the victory. The team is exploring whether the suspension can be appealed under FIFA rules.

cards.headline: England to face Mexico in World Cup round of 16
cards.teaser: England advanced from the group stage and will play Mexico in the knockout round after both teams progressed.
cards.body:
England will face Mexico in the World Cup round of 16 after completing the group stage. The matchup pits England against a Mexican side that also advanced from their group.

England defeated DR Congo in their previous match but faced difficulties during the game. Tactical analysis of that victory has highlighted areas where England struggled and potential lessons for the team heading into the Mexico match.

cards.headline: England defeats DR Congo to advance in World Cup
cards.teaser: England secured a victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo despite facing challenges during the match.
cards.body:
England defeated DR Congo in a tense World Cup match in Atlanta, coming from behind to advance to the round of 16. Harry Kane scored twice in the victory, securing England's progression from the group stage.

England will face Mexico in the last-16 encounter. Mexico advanced by ending a 40-year knockout drought, having failed to progress past the group stage in their previous seven attempts from 1994 to 2018.

cards.headline: NHL free agency opens with multiple signings
cards.teaser: The 2026 NHL free agency period began with teams signing unrestricted free agents and international players.
cards.body:
NHL teams began signing free agents as the 2026 unrestricted free agency period opened. Multiple players signed contracts on the first day, including international players joining NHL rosters.

Free agent trackers are monitoring the signings and providing grades on the contracts. A number of top free agents remain unsigned and available on the market.

hero.headline: Victor Willis, Village People Frontman and Y.M.C.A. Co-Writer, Dies at 74
hero.body:
Victor Willis, the original lead singer of the Village People and co-writer of the disco anthem Y.M.C.A., has died at 74. The group announced that Willis passed away on Monday, June 30, 2026, following "a short but aggressive illness."

Willis joined the Village People in 1977 after being discovered by French producer Jacques Morali while performing on Broadway. Morali had conceived the group as a concept band based on American stereotypes, telling his lawyer: "We have an idea to put together a very special group, very American and very happy." Willis performed as a naval officer or policeman as part of the band's distinctive costume concept.

As the group's frontman during its peak years, Willis helped create some of disco's most enduring hits. The 1978 single Y.M.C.A. became a global phenomenon, reaching number one in 17 countries. The band followed with other major successes including Macho Man and In the Navy. Despite widespread interpretation of these songs as gay anthems, Willis refuted this characterization and threatened legal action against news organizations making such claims. "That is a false assumption based on the fact that my writing partner was gay, and some (not all) of Village People were gay," he stated in 2024.

Willis left the Village People in 1980 as the group prepared for the poorly received feature film Can't Stop the Music. He briefly returned for the 1982 album Fox on the Box before departing again the following year. A solo album he recorded in 1979 remained unreleased until 2015.

After leaving the music industry, Willis struggled with substance abuse and legal troubles for decades. In 1993, he was charged with rape and assault but was acquitted. He faced multiple drug and firearms arrests beginning in 2005, including possession of cocaine and a handgun. Following probation violations and a string of offenses, a judge granted him leniency in 2006, citing his "potential which remains untapped," and sent him to the Betty Ford rehabilitation clinic in California.

Willis maintained a complicated relationship with Y.M.C.A.'s adoption at political rallies. He initially approved its use for Donald Trump's 2020 presidential campaign but retracted his support as the Black Lives Matter movement gained prominence. He later reversed his position again, acknowledging that Trump's use of the track had "greatly benefited the song," even as he stated his ideological opposition to the president and his support for Kamala Harris in 2024. The Village People performed at Trump's second inauguration events in 2025.

Willis was born on July 1, 1951, in Texas and grew up singing in his father's Baptist church. He met his future wife, actress Phylicia Rashad, while both starred in the Broadway musical The Wiz. They were married from 1978 to the early 1980s.

cards.headline: Josh Gad Joins Margot Robbie and Bradley Cooper in Oceans Prequel
cards.teaser: The actor has signed on for a significant role in the period heist film being developed at Warner Bros.
cards.body:
Josh Gad has joined the cast of the upcoming Oceans 11 prequel, taking a significant role alongside Margot Robbie and Bradley Cooper. The Warner Bros. project is being directed by Cooper, who is also starring in the film.

The period heist film features a growing ensemble cast led by Robbie and Cooper. Casting for additional roles continues as the studio assembles the crew for the prequel to the popular franchise.

cards.headline: Minions and Monsters Opens to Over $13 Million on Wednesday
cards.teaser: The third installment in the Minions franchise launched with strong opening day numbers at the domestic box office.
cards.body:
Minions and Monsters earned more than $13 million in its Wednesday opening at U.S. theaters. The film represents the third entry in the Minions franchise and features voice work from Jesse Eisenberg, Jeff Bridges, and Zoey Deutch.

The movie's release includes the return of Pierre Coffin as the voice of the Minions, using the fictional Minionese language he created for the characters. The opening day performance positions the film for a significant weekend at the box office.

cards.headline: Cardi B Awarded $60,000 in Dispute With Blogger Tasha K
cards.teaser: The rapper won additional damages from the blogger over posts about Offset and Stefon Diggs that violated a previous settlement.
cards.body:
Cardi B has won a $60,000 award against blogger Tasha K over social media posts concerning Offset and NFL player Stefon Diggs. The rapper claimed the posts violated terms of a previous settlement agreement between the two parties.

This latest legal action follows Cardi B's $4 million defamation victory against Tasha K in 2022. The new award addresses specific posts that allegedly breached the conditions of that earlier settlement.

cards.headline: Autopsy Report Released for Wire Actor James Ransone
cards.teaser: New details about the actor's death have been disclosed through medical examiner records.
cards.body:
The medical examiner's report for James Ransone, known for his role in The Wire, has been released with additional information about his death. The report indicates the actor had been taking medications and showed evidence of mental health challenges.

Ransone died by suicide. The coroner's report did not include a suicide note among the findings. The actor was recognized for his work on the acclaimed HBO series and other film and television projects.

cards.headline: T.I. and Tiny Win No Punitive Damages in OMG Girlz Case
cards.teaser: A jury declined to restore the $53.6 million in punitive damages that had been previously thrown out by a California judge.
cards.body:
T.I. and Tiny were awarded zero dollars in punitive damages in their trial involving the OMG Girlz. The jury's decision left intact a judge's earlier ruling that had eliminated $53.6 million in punitive damages.

The couple had sought to restore the substantial punitive award through the trial in California. The jury's verdict concluded that portion of the case without additional damages being granted.

cards.headline: Rosalía's Lux Tour Performs at Los Angeles Kia Forum
cards.teaser: The Spanish singer-songwriter brought her elaborate stage show to the Los Angeles venue on Monday night.
cards.body:
Rosalía performed at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles as part of her Lux tour. The show featured the artist's signature blend of music and visual spectacle, including a guest appearance by another performer.

The Monday night concert followed the format established on the Lux tour, which includes dialogue segments with guest stars. The Spanish singer-songwriter has been touring in support of her recent work.

hero.headline: EPA approves three pesticides containing carbon-fluorine bonds
hero.body:
The Environmental Protection Agency approved three new pesticides this week that contain molecules with carbon-fluorine bonds, which can be difficult to break down over time. The approvals have raised questions about whether these chemicals fall under international definitions of forever chemicals, though the EPA disputes that characterization.

Carbon-fluorine bonds are known for their strength and resistance to breakdown in the environment. The agency's approval of pesticides containing these molecular structures comes as concerns about persistent chemicals in the environment continue to grow nationwide.

The EPA has pushed back against labeling these newly approved pesticides as forever chemicals. The agency's position reflects an ongoing dispute over how these substances should be classified and regulated under current environmental standards.

The three pesticides join a growing number of chemical products approved for agricultural and commercial use despite questions about their long-term environmental persistence. The approvals were issued by the Trump administration's EPA.

Forever chemicals, formally known as PFAS, have become a significant environmental concern because they do not easily break down in nature and can accumulate in water supplies, soil, and human bodies over time. International definitions of these substances often include any chemicals with strong carbon-fluorine bonds, which makes them resistant to natural degradation processes.

cards.headline: Kelly backs former admiral fired by Hegseth in congressional race
cards.teaser: Senator Mark Kelly endorsed Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral removed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who is running for Congress in South Carolina.
cards.body:
Senator Mark Kelly of Arizona endorsed Democrat Nancy Lacore on Wednesday for a House seat representing South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. Lacore is a three-star admiral who served as Chief of Navy Reserve before Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired her last year.

Lacore is running to replace Rep. Nancy Mace in the House. Her military leadership experience in the Navy Reserve's highest position would be brought to Congress if elected.

cards.headline: California bans sell by labels on food products
cards.teaser: A new state law took effect Wednesday requiring food manufacturers to use standardized labels indicating quality and safety instead of sell by dates.
cards.body:
California implemented a law Wednesday that prohibits sell by labels on food products as part of an effort to reduce food waste statewide. Food manufacturers must now use one or both of two standardized labels: best if used by to indicate peak quality, and use by to indicate product safety.

The law aims to reduce confusion among consumers about when food is still safe to eat versus when it has passed its peak freshness. Standardizing date labels is intended to prevent edible food from being discarded unnecessarily, addressing both waste and cost concerns.

cards.headline: Pritzker accuses Trump of dementia on CNN
cards.teaser: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker said President Trump is suffering from dementia during a CNN interview discussing recent presidential statements.
cards.body:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker accused President Trump of suffering from dementia during a CNN appearance on Tuesday. Anchor Kaitlan Collins prompted the comments by asking Pritzker about recent statements Trump made, including claims that communism represents a greater threat to the United States than both world wars, the Pearl Harbor attack, and September 11 combined.

Pritzker's remarks constitute a direct personal attack on Trump's mental fitness from a prominent Democratic governor. The comments emerged as Trump prepared to deliver a July 4 address celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Trump plans long July 4 speech despite forecast of 107-degree heat
cards.teaser: The president said Wednesday he will deliver an extended address on the National Mall for the 250th birthday despite extreme temperature predictions.
cards.body:
President Trump said Wednesday that he will deliver a long speech on the National Mall for the July 4 celebration of America's 250th birthday, acknowledging the extreme heat forecast even as he committed to going ahead with the extended address.

The National Mall speech is part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of American independence.

cards.headline: Trump visited Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in North Dakota
cards.teaser: The president toured the new library Wednesday and interacted with an artificial intelligence version of the former president.
cards.body:
President Trump visited Medora, North Dakota on Wednesday to dedicate the new Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, a $450 million facility honoring the 26th president. The library is located in the region where Theodore Roosevelt lived as a cowboy and big-game hunter during the 1880s.

During his tour, Trump interacted with an artificial intelligence version of Theodore Roosevelt as part of the library's experience. The visit was part of Trump's 250th anniversary tour across the country.

cards.headline: Trump financial disclosure shows over $2 billion in income
cards.teaser: The president's 2025 financial disclosure revealed income from various sources, including hundreds of millions from a cryptocurrency venture.
cards.body:
President Trump earned more than $2.2 billion in 2025, according to a financial disclosure released Tuesday by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics. Cryptocurrency ventures, particularly World Liberty Financial which Trump and his sons helped launch, generated over $1 billion of that total since he returned to the White House.

The disclosure reveals Trump's income came from a diverse global network of businesses and investments, with crypto enterprises now eclipsing much of his property portfolio. The filing has raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest given his current position.
